title: Chirped Contact Resonance for Enhanced Simultaneous Nanoscale IR and Mechanical Property Measurements
content: Atomic Force Microscopists have long benefited from property mapping modes such as Force Volume and PeakForce Tapping which provide force curves (force spectra) at each pixel of the scan area. These modes allow detailed mechanical characterization of the sample while controlling the lateral forces that can damage the probe tip and/or sample. When a hold segment during which a fixed force is applied is inserted between the approach and retract, even more possibilities arise [1]. For example, an electrical bias might be ramped, providing multi-dimensional data cubes whereby both electrical & mechanical spectra are present for each pixel. Other examples include application of a single frequency (AFM-nDMA) [2] or a chirped frequency sweep (CR-AFM) [3] for additional mechanical characterization.
